description: The image displays three pie charts, each representing the distribution of different categories across three difficulty levels—easy, medium, and hard—presumably related to performance or outcomes in a knowledge reasoning task involving large language models. The leftmost chart, labeled "easy," shows three segments: a teal segment at 55.4%, a yellow segment at 38.3%, and a red segment at 1.7%, with a small orange segment at 4.6% (likely a mislabeled or misaligned value). The middle chart, labeled "medium," features a teal segment at 58.8%, a yellow segment at 35.4%, and a red segment at 1.8%, with a small orange segment at 4.0%. The rightmost chart, labeled "hard," includes a teal segment at 18.1%, a yellow segment at 37.3%, an orange segment at 37.9%, and a red segment at 6.7%. A legend on the right side of the image indicates that the colors correspond to different conditions: teal for N, yellow for N–K+, orange for N–K–, and red for N+K–. The charts are arranged horizontally, with the "easy" and "medium" labels positioned above their respective charts, and the "hard" label partially visible above the rightmost chart. The labels "Zero-Shot" and "One-Shot" are visible below the middle chart, suggesting that the data may represent performance under different prompting strategies. The percentages are clearly labeled within each slice of the pie charts, and the visual emphasis on the largest segments suggests a focus on the dominant categories within each difficulty level.
